assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework supplied the central modern language for monetary-policy analysis, with profound academic and practical influence.
assessment.attribution: Calvo, Taylor and Woodford represent foundational pricing, policy-rule and welfare-based theoretical contributions, though the listed research program is substantially broader than three people.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been tested, extended and used in policy analysis over several decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of the program makes a three-person attribution necessarily incomplete.
The relative importance of its constituent models and policy applications remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models linking collateral values, borrower balance sheets and aggregate fluctuations transformed the analysis of credit-driven macroeconomic amplification.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the core collateral-constraint mechanism, while Gertler is central to financial-accelerator formulations; Gilchrist is also an important contributor to the stated body of work.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism has shaped macro-finance research and crisis-era policy discussion for many years.
uncertainties: Empirical magnitudes of financial amplification vary across settings.
Attribution between overlapping collateral and financial-accelerator literatures is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection gave trade theory a powerful account of why trade reallocates activity across firms and affects aggregate productivity and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical heterogeneous-firm model; Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply incorporated into contemporary trade research and has generated a large empirical literature.
uncertainties: The canonical contribution is especially closely associated with one scholar, complicating a shared award.
Quantitative implications depend on assumptions about firm responses and market structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern political economics made institutions, electoral incentives and state capacity analytically central to fiscal policy and long-run development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini established much of the formal comparative-institutions program, with Besley making foundational contributions on accountability, public finance and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda is longstanding, widely used and influential across public, development and macroeconomic research.
uncertainties: The candidate label joins several distinct literatures rather than a single discrete discovery.
Institutional causal effects are empirically context-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification reframed credible empirical inference by making transparent what conclusions survive weak and realistic assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski supplied the foundational program, while Tamer and Molinari developed influential methods for moment inequalities and applied partial-identification analysis.
assessment.maturity: The approach has matured into a durable part of econometric theory and empirical practice.
uncertainties: The foundational intellectual credit is unevenly concentrated in Manski.
Its practical uptake is less universal than point-identification methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression provided a fundamental tool for studying conditional distributions and heterogeneity rather than only conditional means.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the clear originators of the core method; Chernozhukov has made major later contributions to distributional econometrics.
assessment.maturity: The method has had several decades of theoretical development and wide use across economics and adjacent fields.
uncertainties: The appropriate inclusion of later distributional-method contributors is debatable.
The contribution may be viewed as a methodological tool rather than a sufficiently unified economic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation literature supplied a persuasive quantitative framework for relating distorted resource allocation to productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the prominent measurement framework, with Restuccia making foundational related contributions to misallocation and development.
assessment.maturity: It has generated sustained theoretical and empirical work and remains central in research on productivity differences.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect forces other than inefficient distortions.
The size of implied aggregate gains is sensitive to modeling and measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion changed the modeling and experimental study of economic behavior and institutions.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is a central architect of the experimental and behavioral evidence; Falk and Schmidt made major complementary contributions, including influential formalization of inequity aversion.
assessment.maturity: The body of evidence and theory has accumulated over decades and strongly influenced behavioral, labor and organizational economics.
uncertainties: Behavioral effects and their external validity vary by context.
Credit is distributed across a broad experimental and theoretical literature.
